# Day Activity Centre (DAC) - SupportGoWhere

Day Activity Centre (DAC)

Share link

Community-based facilities that provide care and skills training to persons with disabilities aged 18 and above to maximise their independence.

SERVICE HIGHLIGHTS

- Centre-based
- Fees payable
- Referral required

Service Providers

Find service providers near you

Expand all sections

About this support

- The DACs' programme is designed to equip persons with disabilities with daily living skills and community living skills to maximise their independence.

- The activities also aim to meaningfully occupy persons with disabilities with social and recreational activities.

- Therapeutic and behavioural intervention services may be provided at some centres.

- DACs also provide a form of respite for caregivers during the day.


Who is this for?

Applicants should be:

- 18 years old and above\*^#

- Singapore citizens or Permanent Residents^^

- Have a permanent disability based on any one of the following:

  - Physical Disability: Requires some assistance with at least 1 of the 6 Activities of Daily Living due to physical impairment

  - A visual impairment: Moderate visual impairment or worse in the better eye

  - A hearing impairment: Moderate hearing loss or worse in the better ear

  - Intellectual disability

  - Autism

Proof of disability must be provided using the [Disability Verification Form](https://www.enablingguide.sg/disability-verification)\\*\\* completed by a relevant registered healthcare professional.

- Applicants should not be suffering from any untreated infectious disease.


\*Students of Government and community-funded SPED schools should be encouraged to remain in school until graduation. Parents of SPED graduands may approach their School to discuss the transition plans of the children prior to graduating from School.

^Applicants who are below age 21 will need consent of parents or legal guardians for their application.

#Applicants who are aged 21 and above with no mental capacity, will need the consent of the appointed deputy(s)/donee(s) on behalf of the applicant.

^^For Permanent Residents, at least one immediate family member must be a Singapore Citizen. Immediate family members refer to spouses, parents, children or the applicant, including stepparents and stepchildren.

\*\*From 8 September 2025, the [Disability Verification Form (DVF)](https://www.enablingguide.sg/disability-verification) is the standardised proof of disability required to verify an individual’s disability status when applying for selected MSF disability schemes and services and other selected Government schemes. Applicants can check if their disability status is already verified via their Touchpoints, SupportGoWhere, or call SG Enable at [1800-8585-885](tel:1800-8585-885)

What to expect?

- SG Enable will contact you within 10 working days upon receiving the completed application together with the required supporting documents from the touchpoint. SG Enable will also update the social worker who assisted in the application on the status of the application.

- Acceptance into the programme at the preferred centre is subject to the availability of vacancies and approval of the centre management.


How to apply?

- Please approach a social service professional from a touchpoint (e.g. Social Service Agency (SSA), hospitals etc.) for assistance in submitting a DAC application. If you are currently not receiving support from any social service or medical touchpoints, you may [approach SG Enable for assistance](https://www.enablingguide.sg/im-looking-for-disability-support/child-adult-care/information-and-referral-services).

- Before meeting your Touchpoints, all applicants are encouraged to check if your disability status has already been verified by logging into [SupportGoWhere](https://supportgowhere.life.gov.sg/grants/pwdr/apply) with your Singpass. If you do not have a verified disability status, the Touchpoint will guide you to the relevant registered healthcare professionals to assist with DVF.


**Submission of applications to SG Enable by Social Service Professional (Online or Hardcopy)**

**Step 1:**

All applicants should check if they have a verified disability status by logging into [SupportGoWhere](https://supportgowhere.life.gov.sg/grants/pwdr/apply) with their Singpass. If the applicant already has a verified disability status, a DVF is not required.

**Step 2:**

If the applicant does not have a verified disability status or has a new disability condition which has not been verified previously, registered Touchpoint Assessor/Admin must submit a copy of the DVF completed by a relevant registered Healthcare Professional together with the AD application.

**Step 3:**

Registered touchpoints’ Assessor/Admin may submit clients’ AD application and completed DVF online via CorpPass (recommended) or via hardcopy.

1. **Online submission (Recommended)**

Log into e-Services using your CorpPass

2. **Hardcopy submission**

Download the [AD application form](https://www.enablingguide.sg/docs/default-source/default-document-library/ad-application-form.pdf?sfvrsn=71d5f444_3), print and send together with the required documents. If required, you may download sections of the AD application form and DVF below for use:

   - [Client Assessment Form (Revised)](https://www.enablingguide.sg/docs/default-source/default-document-library/final-caf-r-form.pdf?sfvrsn=c2d096c3_1)

   - [Medical Information Form](https://www.enablingguide.sg/docs/default-source/default-document-library/final-interim-medical-information.pdf?sfvrsn=c4f804d4_1)

   - [Declaration Form](https://www.enablingguide.sg/docs/default-source/default-document-library/declaration-form.pdf?sfvrsn=a7fa3568_2)

   - [Disability Verification Form](https://www.enablingguide.sg/disability-verification)
